IBS-D is a chronic functional disorder and does not present with acute, high-frequency diarrhea over two days—its episodic nature and lack of systemic features make it unlikely in this acute presentation, hence low confidence (0.32). No red flags (e.g., fever, blood, dehydration, immunocompromise) are reported, further narrowing the differential toward common community-acquired pathogens."}

Other entities (e.g., Shigella, Yersinia, viral adenovirus) were considered but ranked lower due to lower epidemiologic probability or atypical features (e.g., Shigella often has fever/bloody stool; Yersinia may present with right-sided pain mimicking appendicitis)."}
